skill.name: architecture-synthesis
skill.description: Generates reference architecture specifications for agent frameworks, including primitives, protocols, execution loops, diagrams, and implementation roadmaps.
skill.summary: Synthesize agent framework architecture from prior analysis and design requirements.

content.value_statement: Designing an agent framework requires clear primitives, interfaces, and execution rules. This skill turns prior analysis into a reference architecture and implementation roadmap.
actual_capabilities: Defines Message, AgentState, ToolResult, AgentFinish, and AgentContinue primitives.
Specifies LLM, Tool, and Memory protocols with clear method responsibilities.
Outlines an agent execution loop with parsing, tool execution, events, and step limits.
Provides a Mermaid architecture diagram for core, protocol, execution, and integration layers.
Creates phased implementation roadmap and expected documentation artifacts.
limitations: Does not inspect a codebase or generate runnable project files by itself.
Assumes comparative analysis, anti-patterns, and requirements are already available.
Examples are Python-oriented and may need adaptation for other languages.
Does not validate provider APIs, credentials, or production infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Agent Framework
use_cases.description: Turn framework research into a concrete architecture with primitives, interfaces, and execution flow.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Interfaces
use_cases.description: Define shared contracts for LLM calls, tools, memory, results, and callbacks before implementation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Implementation Work
use_cases.description: Convert design decisions into phased milestones, documentation artifacts, and example deliverables.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use architecture-synthesis to draft a reference architecture for a simple agent framework. Include primitives, protocols, loop design, and roadmap.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Requirements to Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use architecture-synthesis with my requirements and comparative matrix. Highlight which primitives, interfaces, and execution rules satisfy each requirement.

prompt_templates.title: Design Extension Points
prompt_templates.prompt: Use architecture-synthesis to define extension points for tools, memory, callbacks, streaming, and error handling in an agent framework.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize Production Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use architecture-synthesis to create a production-ready architecture brief. Include provider integrations, observability, failure modes, implementation phases, and validation criteria.

output_examples.input: A team has selected common agent design patterns and needs a reference architecture.
output_examples.output: A document with primitive definitions, protocol responsibilities, an execution-loop narrative, a layer diagram, and a phased roadmap.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead wants consistent tool, memory, and LLM interfaces before coding.
output_examples.output: A set of interface descriptions, method responsibilities, expected results, and integration boundaries for the implementation team.

output_examples.input: A product manager needs implementation milestones for an agent framework MVP.
output_examples.output: A roadmap covering core types, provider integration, robustness work, extensibility, production readiness, and documentation deliverables.

best_practices: Provide the comparative matrix, anti-pattern catalog, and design requirements before using the skill.
Review generated primitives and protocols with implementers before starting production code.
Treat diagrams and roadmap phases as planning artifacts, then validate them against real constraints.
anti_patterns: Do not use the architecture as a security review or production readiness assessment.
Do not skip requirements and ask for a full framework design from vague goals.
Do not assume the Python examples directly fit every runtime or language.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a reference architecture with primitives, protocols, execution flow, diagrams, roadmap, and expected artifacts.

faq.question: Does it write implementation code?
faq.answer: It provides templates and pseudocode, but it does not create a complete runnable framework.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Use a comparative framework matrix, anti-pattern list, and clear design requirements.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is it limited to Python?
faq.answer: The examples use Python-style types, but the architecture concepts can be adapted to other languages.

faq.question: Does it make security decisions?
faq.answer: No. It describes architecture structure and should be paired with separate security and threat modeling work.
